title: bug: the blocked-timeout sweep times a silent BLOCKED seat out as a corpse, but its IDLE write stamps a fresh lastActivityAt, unlike its two sibling seat clears (REVIEW self-heal, reconcile-window sweep). So the corpse reads alive for 120 s, a restart in that window spares it, and the same pass's Layer-3 prune slips by a full staleWorkerTimeoutMs
description:
Filed by hunt #14 (task-d5d58972, 2026-11-03, architect-1dd28c7c). Lane: dead-worker handling. This is one write skipping a convention its two siblings document and apply.

PROBLEM (HEAD 942717bc)
- The convention:
  - workerStore.updateWorker (packages/moe-daemon/src/state/workerStore.ts:176-188) stamps lastActivityAt = now on every non-DEAD update "unless the caller passes an explicit lastActivityAt (system-side repairs like the REVIEW self-heal, which must not gift a crashed worker a fresh heartbeat and resurrect it as alive)".
  - packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md:7: presence (isWorkerAlive, 120 s) is display-only, and records are pruned once they own nothing.
- The two sibling seat clears in state/sweeps.ts follow it:
  - the reconcile-window sweep, :290-298: `updateWorker(owner.id, { currentTaskId: null, lastActivityAt: owner.lastActivityAt })`. Its comment says a fresh stamp "would resurrect a suspected corpse as alive and defeat the Layer-3 prune that removes it once it owns nothing";
  - the REVIEW self-heal, :515-525, the same pattern.
- The blocked-timeout does not. Its IDLE write, sweeps.ts:485-489, is `updateWorker(worker.id, { status: 'IDLE', lastError: null, currentTaskId: null }, 'WORKER_TIMEOUT')`, with no lastActivityAt. So the seat it has just judged a corpse (silent past blockedTimeoutMs, 1 h) gets lastActivityAt = now.
- Effects:
  - The corpse reads alive (isWorkerAlive) for 120 s in list_workers and chat_who. The architect page in report_blocked (findFreshestLiveWorkerByRole) can pick a timed-out architect in that window.
  - A daemon restart in that window spares the record as recently active (purgeAllWorkers).
  - The Layer-3 prune at the end of the same pass (sweeps.ts:567-584) skips it, so the record lingers another staleWorkerTimeoutMs (30 min) even when it owns nothing.

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/zzHuntA_blockedTimeoutHeartbeat.test.ts, run from packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive 942717bc` snapshot.
- Setup: a seat parked BLOCKED by a third-party block and silent 2 h. The real checkBlockedTimeouts runs, and the row is correctly parked to BACKLOG.
- `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/zzHuntA_blockedTimeoutHeartbeat.test.ts` → 1 failed:
  AssertionError: expected '2026-11-03T23:28:21.322Z' to be '2026-11-03T21:28:21.286Z'   (lastActivityAt re-stamped)
  AssertionError: expected true to be false                                              (isWorkerAlive(corpse))
  AssertionError: expected { id: 'worker-walled', …(13) } to be null                       (the same pass's Layer-3 prune skipped it)
- The architect re-ran it at 23:28Z with the same three failures. The output is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-d5d58972/A/blockedTimeoutHeartbeat.vitest.txt.
- Exposure: every blocked-timeout of a silent seat. That is any seat parked BLOCKED (a resource block, or a third-party block on an assigned row) whose wrapper died. The blocked-timeout did not fire in today's activity.log, so this is a guard gap, not a live incident. LOW.

FIX DIRECTION
- One line: pass `lastActivityAt: worker.lastActivityAt` in the IDLE write at sweeps.ts:485-489, exactly as :297 and :523 do.
- The WORKER_TIMEOUT activity event stays.
- Do not change the task writes above it, or the resource or dependency arms.

FILES (planner to confirm)
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/sweeps.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/blockedTimeoutPresence.test.ts (new), or a new case in the existing sweeps.test.ts

OUT OF SCOPE: setTaskStatus.ts and dependencyUnblock.ts (the sibling row task-a133bd6a, no shared file); the sweep's #governors stale-block alert (hunt #11's lane); chat cursor writes on DEAD records (held back, reported to the governor). Docs: no tool contract changes and no doc describes this stamp, so there is nothing to sync.

VERIFICATION (in a git-archive snapshot, never in place): `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/state/sweeps.test.ts src/state/blockedTimeoutPresence.test.ts`

The same test asserts that, when the timed-out seat owns nothing after the park, the same pass's Layer-3 prune removes the record (getWorker returns null), matching the REVIEW self-heal and reconcile-window behaviour.

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 3, the fix, plus the one existing test that pinned the old end state.

(a) In packages/moe-daemon/src/state/sweeps.ts runBlockedTimeoutSweep, the IDLE write (HEAD lines 485-489) gains `lastActivityAt: worker.lastActivityAt,` after `currentTaskId: null,`, with a 3-line comment above the call: "Keep the corpse's real lastActivityAt, as the REVIEW self-heal and the reconcile-window sweep do: a fresh stamp would make it read alive for the presence window and defer the Layer-3 prune below." The whole file must equal sweeps.expected.ts (sha256 fa55ffb6e83570f0dd99793b2b8c36bdd8726ea9f8e959fae7d8b7dc7a567e72). Use the loop's own `worker`, the pre-sweep record, exactly as :297 and :525 use `owner.lastActivityAt`. A re-read of state.workers is equivalent today, because updateTask's prior-owner release (taskStore.ts, shouldClearWorker) runs only when a status change leaves assignedWorkerId unset, and the park sets it to null. The loop variable stays correct even if that changes. Nothing else in the sweep changes: the task writes, the resource and dependency arms, the WORKER_TIMEOUT event, the REVIEW self-heal, the alerts, the reaper and Layer 3 all stay. Error handling: no new failure path. It is the same updateWorker call with one more field. updateWorker throws only for a missing worker, impossible inside this loop over state.workers, and the sweep's existing logging is untouched. The WORKER_TIMEOUT worker event's payload is the updates object, so it now also carries lastActivityAt. That is additive: only schema.ts and tests name the event.

(b) packages/moe-daemon/src/state/dependencyUnblock.test.ts, in 'blocked-worker timeout parks a dep-less BLOCKED hold but keeps a dependency-waiting one BLOCKED — and UNASSIGNS it' (HEAD lines 358-359): replace `// The timed-out worker itself is still released to IDLE.` and `expect(h.state.getWorker('worker-t1meout')!.status).toBe('IDLE');` with the two-line comment "The timed-out seat owns nothing now and keeps its real lastActivityAt (2 h old), so the same pass's Layer-3 prune removes it." and `expect(h.state.getWorker('worker-t1meout')).toBeNull();`. The whole file must equal dependencyUnblock.expected.test.ts (sha256 959b9fa5551cc523ed5d94ad3965e1f9eaaeaea0531e89c58ac1c68ef98a82ff). Why: that seat owns nothing after the sweep and is silent 2 h, past the harness default staleWorkerTimeoutMs of 30 min. With the fix it is pruned in the same pass, exactly DoD 2. With the old assertion, `null!.status` throws, which is the one failure the architect saw. The rest of that test is unchanged and still passes: the dep row unassigned and BLOCKED, the dep-less row in BACKLOG, the restore once the dep is DONE, and worker-fresh1's claim.

The architect ran the full daemon suite in a whole-tree snapshot with exactly these three files: 275 files, 7406 passed, 24 skipped, exit 0. No other test needs a change. GREEN: the new file gives 2 passed in the snapshot.
implementationPlan.note: sweeps.ts IDLE write passes worker.lastActivityAt; dependencyUnblock.test.ts assertion updated. Both byte-identical to reference files (cmp).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the loop's pre-sweep `worker.lastActivityAt`, the sibling pattern at sweeps.ts:297 and :525, rather than re-reading state.workers, which is equivalent today. Put the new cases in a new file: sweeps.test.ts covers the reconcile window, arming and alerts and has no blocked-timeout case, and StateManager.test.ts builds its own fixtures. Hold both seats in one test, one pruned and one kept by a 3 h staleWorkerTimeoutMs, so DoD 1 and DoD 2 are asserted in the same test; a pruned record cannot show its stamp. Add the restart-purge case, because it is one of the three effects the row names and it costs one call. The dependencyUnblock.test.ts assertion has to change: it pinned the old end state (the corpse kept as IDLE) that DoD 2 removes.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: workerStore.updateWorker stamps lastActivityAt = now on every non-DEAD update unless the update carries one. Layer 3 prunes a worker silent past staleWorkerTimeoutMs that holds no active task (isWorkerEligibleForStaleCleanup). purgeAllWorkers keeps workers that are isWorkerAlive (120 s) or hold open attempts. updateTask's prior-owner release runs only when a status change leaves assignedWorkerId unset.
